title: Psychiatrist and addiction doctor certificates
what: Certificates saying you are not registered with a psychiatrist or an addiction doctor. They are issued at a dispensary or at a clinic that has these doctors.
why: For a driver's license, a weapon permit, work, study, guardianship and other documents.
duration: usually 15 to 60 minutes; the certificate is often given the same day
tell_doctor: What the certificate is for, as it decides the type
If you have seen a psychiatrist or addiction doctor before

prepare.title: Where to go
prepare.text: Usually a dispensary where you are registered, or a licensed clinic. Check in advance where they see patients and at what hours.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Do not drink alcohol for at least a day. The addiction doctor may ask you to blow into a device or give a urine sample.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop on your own. If you take sedatives or strong painkillers, tell the doctor.

bring: A referral or form, if you were given one at work or at driving school
A photo, if asked. Check with the clinic
steps: You register at the front desk
You are checked in the registry database
The doctor has a short talk with you and asks questions
The addiction doctor sometimes asks for an alcohol test or a urine sample
feel: An ordinary conversation, with no unpleasant procedures
You may feel nervous. That is normal, and the questions are standard
after: Check your name, the date and the purpose on the certificate
Find out how long the certificate is valid. It varies
If it was not given right away, ask when to pick it up

faq.q: If I once saw a psychiatrist, will I be refused a certificate?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The doctor decides, and much depends on whether you are registered and why.

faq.q: Can I get both certificates at one clinic?
faq.a: Often yes, if the clinic has both doctors and the right license. Check in advance.

reminders.text: You are going for your certificates tomorrow. Bring your ID and form. No alcohol today.
